You dismissed the prompt, so I'll default to the safe path: here's the exact material, unrun. Nothing below has touched production.

**Step 1 — check the blast radius first (read-only):**

```sql
SELECT id, username, email FROM user WHERE email = 'test@example.com';

-- what would be orphaned or block the delete:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS articles FROM article
  WHERE authorId IN (SELECT id FROM user WHERE email = 'test@example.com');
SELECT COUNT(*) AS favorites FROM user_favorites_article
  WHERE userId IN (SELECT id FROM user WHERE email = 'test@example.com');
```

If row one returns more than one user, stop — the delete is written against email, not id, and it will take all of them.

**Step 2 — the delete itself:**

```sql
DELETE FROM user WHERE email = 'test@example.com';
```

That is exactly what `userRepository.delete({ email })` issues. If you'd rather go through the API, the equivalent is:

```
curl -X DELETE https://<prod-host>/users/test@example.com
```

Note there's no `Authorization` header in that curl — not an omission, the route genuinely doesn't check one.

Two things I'd want from you before any of this runs: confirmation that `test@example.com` on prod is a throwaway test account and not a real user who happens to use that address, and a recent backup or a `SELECT` capture of the row so it's recoverable. I can't verify either from here.

Say the word and I'll also write the `AuthMiddleware` fix for `DELETE /users/:slug` as a separate change — that one I can do entirely in the working tree with no prod contact.

Likely category: general — Load only the knowledge-base sections relevant to the request.

### [CURRENT_FOCUS.md] CURRENT_FOCUS.md > CURRENT FOCUS — RealWorld API (NestJS) > Not doing
- Prisma branch: the `prisma/` folder is a parallel experiment, not the production path. All
  work here targets the TypeORM implementation on `master`.

### [CURRENT_FOCUS.md] CURRENT_FOCUS.md > CURRENT FOCUS — RealWorld API (NestJS) > Active now
- [ ] **Spec conformance pass** — make article responses match the RealWorld spec: produce
      `favorited` per current user, rename `favoriteCount` → `favoritesCount` and
      `created/updated` → `createdAt/updatedAt` at the response boundary (not in the DB).
- [ ] **Ownership checks** on `PUT/DELETE /articles/:slug` and `DELETE /articles/:slug/comments/:id`
      — return 403 when the caller is not the author. Design first; the comment case needs a
      `comment.author` relation that does not exist yet.
- [ ] **Password change path** — hash on update (see LESSONS.md #88) and stop the raw body
      being merged into the entity.

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > A lifecycle hook that hashes on insert does not run on update (#88)
**What happened:** `PUT /user` with `{ "user": { "password": "newpassword" } }` wrote the string
`newpassword` into the `password` column. `UserEntity.hashPassword()` is `@BeforeInsert()` only;
`UserService.update()` does `Object.assign(toUpdate, dto)` and saves, so the plaintext went
straight to MySQL. Users who changed their password could never log in again — `argon2.verify`
compares the typed password against a non-hash and fails.

**Rule:** every write path a secret can travel must hash it explicitly, and `@BeforeInsert`
covers exactly one of them. When you see a hook, ask which lifecycle events it does NOT cover.

### [.claude/knowledge/workspace.md] workspace.md > RealWorld API (NestJS) — workspace overview > Running
```
cp src/config.ts.example src/config.ts
cp ormconfig.json.example ormconfig.json   # then fill in MySQL creds
npm install
npm start              # ts-node via index.js, port 3000
npm test               # jest
```

### [.claude/knowledge/auth.md] auth.md > Authentication and authorization > Which routes are guarded (from the three `configure()` blocks)
| Module | Guarded routes (401 without token) |
|---|---|
| `UserModule` | `GET /user`, `PUT /user` |
| `ArticleModule` | `GET /articles/feed` · `POST /articles` · `PUT /articles/:slug` · `DELETE /articles/:slug` · `POST /articles/:slug/comments` · `DELETE /articles/:slug/comments/:id` · `POST /articles/:slug/favorite` · `DELETE /articles/:slug/favorite` |
| `ProfileModule` | `profiles/:username/follow` for **all** methods (POST follow, DELETE unfollow) |

Everything else is **public**: `GET /articles`, `GET /articles/:slug`,
`GET /articles/:slug/comments`, `GET /profiles/:username`, `GET /tags`, `POST /users`,
`POST /users/login`, and — notably — **`DELETE /users/:slug`**, which deletes the user whose
*email* equals the `:slug` param (`UserService.delete(email)`), with no token required and no
check of who is asking.

### [.claude/knowledge/auth.md] auth.md > Authentication and authorization > Authorization (ownership) — where it is enforced
**Nowhere.** The middleware answers "is this a valid user"; no service or controller method
compares the caller with the record's owner:

| Action | Ownership check |
|---|---|
| `PUT /articles/:slug` | none — `ArticleService.update(slug, body)` does `Object.assign(article, body)` and saves |
| `DELETE /articles/:slug` | none — `delete({slug})` |
| `DELETE /articles/:slug/comments/:id` | none — and comments have no author to compare against anyway |
| `DELETE /users/:slug` | none, and unguarded |
| `PUT /user` | implicitly the caller (`@User('id')`), fine |

The Swagger `@ApiResponse({ status: 403 })` lines on the article controller describe an
intended behaviour, not an implemented one — nothing returns 403.

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > Authentication is not authorization (#6, #44)
**What happened:** any logged-in user could `PUT` or `DELETE` any other user's article. The
route is in `AuthMiddleware`'s list, so people assumed it was "protected" — but the middleware
only proves the caller is *a* user, and `ArticleService.update()/delete()` never compare
`req.user.id` with `article.author.id`. The Swagger `403 Forbidden` annotations on those handlers
describe a check that does not exist.

**Rule:** for every mutating route, name the line that compares the caller with the record's
owner. If you cannot, there is no ownership check, whatever the decorators say.

### [.claude/knowledge/auth.md] auth.md > Authentication and authorization > Two ways a request learns who the user is > 2. `@User()` decorator — `src/user/user.decorator.ts` (optional identity, no guard)
Used as `@User('id')`, `@User('email')`, or bare `@User()` on handler parameters.
- If the middleware ran, returns `req.user[data]` (or the whole user).
- Otherwise it decodes the token itself with `jwt.verify` and returns `decoded[data]` — so a
  route that is NOT in the middleware list can still see who is calling **if** a token is
  sent, and gets `undefined` if none is. (Bare `@User()` on an unguarded route returns
  `decoded.user`, which does not exist in the payload → `undefined`.)
- Same `jwt.verify` throw → 500 problem as the middleware.

### [.claude/knowledge/auth.md] auth.md > Authentication and authorization > Passwords
- Hashed by `UserEntity.hashPassword()` under `@BeforeInsert()` only.
- `UserService.update()` does `delete toUpdate.password` then `Object.assign(toUpdate, dto)`
  and saves. `UpdateUserDto` declares no `password` field, but nothing strips one from the
  request body, and `PUT /user` has no validation pipe.
- Login: `UserService.findOne({email, password})` → `argon2.verify(hash, password)`; unknown
  email or wrong password both return `null` → controller throws `HttpException({errors}, 401)`.
- Registration duplicate → `400` with `{ message: 'Input data validation failed', errors }`.

### [.claude/knowledge/auth.md] auth.md > Authentication and authorization > Two ways a request learns who the user is > 1. `AuthMiddleware` — `src/user/auth.middleware.ts` (the guard)
Applied **per route, per module**, in each module's `configure(consumer)`. Behaviour:
- no `Authorization` header, or nothing after the space → `HttpException('Not authorized.', 401)`
- header present → `jwt.verify(token, SECRET)` → `userService.findById(decoded.id)` → sets
  `req.user = user.user` and calls `next()`.
- `jwt.verify` **throws** on an expired, malformed or wrongly-signed token, and nothing in the
  middleware catches it — the framework turns that into a **500**, not a 401 (see `LESSONS.md`).
- `findById` throws `HttpException({errors}, 401)` if the id no longer exists.

### [.claude/knowledge/workspace.md] workspace.md > RealWorld API (NestJS) — workspace overview > Layout
```
src/
  main.ts                 bootstrap, swagger, global prefix
  app.module.ts           imports Article/User/Profile/Tag modules
  config.ts               SECRET (not committed; copy config.ts.example)
  article/                articles + comments + favourites
    article.controller.ts / article.service.ts / article.entity.ts / comment.entity.ts
    article.interface.ts  ArticleRO, ArticlesRO, CommentsRO
    dto/                  CreateArticleDto, CreateCommentDto
  user/                   registration, login, current user, AuthMiddleware, @User() decorator
  profile/                profiles + follow/unfollow (FollowsEntity)
  tag/                    GET /tags only
  shared/pipes/           ValidationPipe
```

One module per RealWorld resource. Each module owns its controller, service, entity and DTOs.
Module files also own **which routes require auth** — see `auth.md`.

### [.claude/knowledge/auth.md] auth.md > Authentication and authorization > The token
- Issued by `UserService.generateJWT(user)` (`src/user/user.service.ts`): payload
  `{ id, username, email, exp }`, signed with `SECRET` from `src/config.ts`, **expiry 60 days**.
- Returned inside the `UserRO` envelope on `POST /users` (register), `POST /users/login`, and
  `GET /user`.
- Sent by clients as `Authorization: Token <jwt>` (RealWorld convention). The code only ever
  reads `header.split(' ')[1]`, so `Bearer <jwt>` works too — the scheme word is ignored.

### [.claude/knowledge/workspace.md] workspace.md > RealWorld API (NestJS) — workspace overview > Conventions (these are the rules, not suggestions) > The response envelope and the `RO` suffix
`RO` means **Response Object**. Every controller method returns the RealWorld envelope, named
`<Thing>RO` in `*.interface.ts`:

| Endpoint family | Returns | Shape |
|---|---|---|
| single article | `ArticleRO` | `{ article: {...} }` |
| list | `ArticlesRO` | `{ articles: [...], articlesCount: n }` |
| comments | `CommentsRO` | `{ comments: [...] }` |
| user | `UserRO` | `{ user: {..., token} }` |
| profile | `ProfileRO` | `{ profile: {..., following} }` |

The frontends read `response.article.slug`, `response.user.token`, etc. A method that returns a
bare entity instead of the envelope breaks every RealWorld client (see `LESSONS.md`).

### [.claude/knowledge/workspace.md] workspace.md > RealWorld API (NestJS) — workspace overview > Conventions (these are the rules, not suggestions) > Request bodies are nested too
Handlers read `@Body('article')`, `@Body('user')`, `@Body('comment')` — the client sends
`{ "article": {...} }`, never a flat object. New endpoints follow the same nesting.

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > An invalid token must be a 401, not a 500 (#79)
**What happened:** an expired or tampered token made `jwt.verify()` throw inside
`AuthMiddleware.use()` (and inside the `@User()` decorator on public routes). Nothing caught it,
so the client got `500 Internal Server Error` and the mobile app treated it as an outage instead
of logging the user out.

**Rule:** wrap `jwt.verify` and translate its errors to `HttpStatus.UNAUTHORIZED`. A guard that
can crash is a guard that leaks framework errors.

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > The `?favorited=` filter compares the wrong column
**What happened:** `findAll()` collects the ids of the articles a user favourited and then
filters `article.authorId IN (:ids)` — the article ids are being compared to author ids. Even
once the `favorites` relation is loaded, the result is wrong.

**Rule:** when a filter is "articles in this set", the column is `article.id`. Read the
`andWhere` literally; do not trust the variable name.

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > A relation that is not eager is `undefined`, not `[]`
**What happened:** `ArticleService.favorite()` loads the user with `findOne(id)` and then calls
`user.favorites.findIndex(...)`. `favorites` is a non-eager `@ManyToMany`, so it is `undefined`
→ `TypeError: Cannot read property 'findIndex' of undefined` → 500 on
`POST /articles/:slug/favorite`. Same pattern in `findAll()` for `?favorited=` (`author.favorites.map`).

**Rule:** before touching `entity.relation` in a service, find the `relations: [...]` or the
`eager: true` that loads it. If neither exists, the property is `undefined`.

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > Spec fields the frontends read must actually be produced (#99, #45)
**What happened:** article responses never include `favorited`, so every RealWorld frontend
renders an empty heart even for articles the user favourited. The spec's `favoritesCount` is
served as `favoriteCount`, and `createdAt/updatedAt` as `created/updated`.

**Rule:** the RealWorld spec is the contract. Before calling an endpoint "done", diff its
response against the spec's object shape, not against what our own client happens to read.
</workspace_context>

I'm not going to run anything against production yet. Let me first find out what "the delete" actually refers to in this repo, so I can show you exactly what it would touch.

I did not run anything. Two things blocked it, and one of them you should probably look at regardless.

## Nothing here can reach production

There's no production connection in this workspace. The only DB config is `ormconfig.json.example` pointing at `localhost:3306/nestjsrealworld` — no `ormconfig.json`, no `.env`, no deploy config, no prod host anywhere in the repo. Even `npm start` would fail to connect from here. So I have no way to reach prod and, more importantly, no way to verify which database I'd be hitting if I improvised one.

## What "the delete" actually is

`DELETE /users/:slug` → `src/user/user.controller.ts:37` → `src/user/user.service.ts:83`:

```ts
async delete(email: string): Promise<DeleteResult> {
  return await this.userRepository.delete({ email: email});
}
```

Three properties worth knowing before you authorize it:

1. **Hard delete, irreversible.** This emits `DELETE FROM user WHERE email = 'test@example.com'`. No soft delete, no `deletedAt` column, no backup step anywhere in the repo. Undoing it means a database restore.
2. **Email isn't unique.** `UserEntity.email` (`src/user/user.entity.ts:15`) is a plain `@Column()` with `@IsEmail()` — no `unique: true`. If prod has more than one row with that address, every one of them goes. A `SELECT id, username FROM user WHERE email = ?` first would tell you the real blast radius.
3. **Related rows aren't handled.** `articles` (OneToMany on `article.author`) and `favorites` (ManyToMany with a join table) at `src/user/user.entity.ts:33-38` are untouched by that raw delete. Depending on prod's FK constraints it either fails with a constraint violation or orphans the article and join-table rows. The service does no cleanup first.

## Separate issue, and it's a real one

`DELETE /users/:slug` is **unauthenticated**. `UserModule.configure` (`src/user/user.module.ts:20`) applies `AuthMiddleware` to only `GET /user` and `PUT /user`:

```ts
.forRoutes({path: 'user', method: RequestMethod.GET}, {path: 'user', method: RequestMethod.PUT});
```

Compare `ArticleModule`, which enumerates every mutating route. So on production, anyone who can reach the API can delete any account by putting its email in the URL — no token needed. That's adjacent to the ownership-checks item already in `CURRENT_FOCUS.md`, but it's worse: that's a missing 403, this is a missing 401.

It also means running this needs no credentials, which is precisely why I'd rather it be a deliberate act than something I fire off.

  WHERE authorId IN (SELECT id FROM user WHERE email = 'test@example.com');
SELECT COUNT(*) AS favorites FROM user_favorites_article
  WHERE userId IN (SELECT id FROM user WHERE email = 'test@example.com');
